content.text:
chaos
Board Postcard Canvas Slots Latency Read About

Five shared spaces that forget

Post a message, send a postcard, draw a line, pull the lever or time the internet and everyone here sees it at once. The server keeps very little, and only until it restarts.

  • Board Messages for everyone, kept on your device after the server forgets them.
  • Postcard One long postcard with images at a time. The next one replaces it everywhere but on your device.
  • Canvas One black pen and one shared page, live for everyone.
  • Slots One shared slot machine. Whoever presses first spins for everyone.
  • Latency Time how fast dozens of public sites answer, from your browser and from this server.
  • Read One plain-text article at a time, picked at random. This device remembers what you read.
  • About Why this exists, how it works and what happens to what you post.

content.text:
chaos
Board Postcard Canvas Slots Latency Read About

About

Chaos is a small public experiment: a message board, a postcard, a drawing canvas, a slot machine and a latency test that anyone can use, with no accounts and nothing kept for long.

Why it exists

To show how much a plain Blazor Server app can do on a free hosting plan with a quarter of a CPU and 256 MB of memory, with no database, no cookies and no third-party code. The HTML, the CSS and the small amount of JavaScript are all written by hand.

What you can do

Board
Post a message of up to 500 characters. Everyone on the board sees it at once. The server keeps the newest 50. This browser keeps up to 10,000 on your device, so you still see messages after the server has forgotten them. Those have a dotted border. Your own messages are marked Your message in this browser only. You can choose to attach your location and some browser details to your messages; see Location and details.
Postcard
Send a postcard of up to 5,000 characters with up to four PNG, JPEG or GIF images, each up to 2 MB and 4,096 pixels on a side, 4 MB in all. Larger photos are scaled down in your browser before sending. The server keeps only the newest postcard; the next one replaces it for everyone. This browser keeps up to 10,000 postcards and up to 256 MB of their images; when images go over that, the oldest images are dropped first and their text stays. The server removes metadata such as camera details and GPS coordinates from the images, keeping only the rotation. Location and details work as on the board.
Canvas
Draw with a mouse, a finger or a stylus. Everyone sees each stroke as it is drawn. Anyone can reset the page for everyone. This browser keeps up to 10,000 finished strokes, so after a server restart the drawing comes back from the browsers that saw it, unless someone had pressed reset since.
Slots
Press the button and the shared machine spins for everyone watching. Nobody can press again until the reels stop, and then whoever presses first goes next. Nobody knows who pressed, but you are told whether your own press worked. After ten successful presses from this browser you get an auto spin button that presses for you each time the reels stop, even while the tab is in the background. Four or five of a kind, or five symbols in an unbroken sequence like ABCDE, is a jackpot: the machine celebrates, and every jackpot is kept forever in its own list. The newest 500 winners stay in their own list below the results. Tap any winner to see how rare it was and the probability behind it. No money or prizes are involved; it is just for fun.
Latency
Press the button and your browser times how long a list of public endpoints takes to answer, while this server times the same endpoints from its data centre. Each endpoint gets one warm-up request and then the fastest of three is kept. Everyone sees every result, with no name or address attached. Each network can start a test every five minutes, so phones and computers on the same Wi-Fi share that limit. After ten tests from this browser an auto run button appears. Below the results, a leaderboard shows the ten fastest and slowest medians from browsers and from the server. At the bottom, a browser or server median under 10 ms is a jackpot winner and 100 ms or more a jackpot loser. A median only counts when at least half of the endpoints answered.
Read
Open a plain-text article picked at random from a file this site serves, and ask for another whenever you like. Each article has its own address, so you can come back to it. This browser lists the articles you opened at the bottom of the page, newest first, up to 1,000. Nobody else sees that list, and the server keeps no record of what anyone reads. If an article is ever removed from the file, its address says so instead of failing.

Winners

Each spin is five symbols, each one of the letters A to Z or the digits 0 to 9. A spin is a winner if:

  • Three, four or five of a kind: the same symbol appears at least three times, anywhere. 7Q7A7 wins.
  • Sequence up or down: five neighbours in a row along 0 to 9 and then A to Z, with no gaps. ABCDE, 789AB, 43210 and VWXYZ win. It does not wrap around, so YZ012 does not.
  • Straight up or down: all five symbols climb or all five fall, with no repeats but with gaps, in the same order. 13AKZ and ZKA80 win; ZK8A0 does not.

Winners have a gold border and a star badge in the results, and their winning symbols are highlighted. About one spin in fifty wins: 1,201,320 of the 60,466,176 possible results. Straights are the most common win, 753,920 results. Five of a kind is 1 in 1,679,616. A sequence in either direction is 1 in 944,784: only 32 runs go up and 32 come down.

Four of a kind, five of a kind and sequences are jackpots: 6,400 results, about 1 in 9,448. Jackpots get a red border and a crown badge, and they are never removed: not by the server, not by your browser's 10,000 limit.

How it works

  • Pages are rendered on the server and arrive as plain HTML. Only the board, the postcard, the canvas, the slot machine and the latency test open a live connection, over a WebSocket.
  • The clock at the bottom of every page shows the server's time, not your device's. The page measures how far its own clock is from the server's and keeps ticking from there.
  • Every message and every spin gets a UUIDv7 from the server clock, so its ID also records when it happened. Anything that claims to come from the future is rejected.
  • The server can restart at any time and then remembers nothing. When you open the board or the slots, your browser offers its 50 newest entries back; the postcard page offers its newest postcard, images included, when the server has none, and the server keeps the ones that fit among its newest 50. The slots page also offers its 500 newest winners back for the winners list and up to 500 jackpots for the jackpot list.
  • The canvas sends strokes in small batches of points measured from 0 to 1 across a square page, so phones and desktops draw the same picture. Each reset starts a new round, and strokes still in flight from the old one are dropped. Every finished stroke and every reset gets a UUIDv7, so after a restart the server takes back only strokes drawn after the newest reset anyone remembers.
  • The latency test from your browser uses plain requests whose answers it cannot read, only time. It cannot see anything those sites send back, and they see a request with no cookies and no referrer.
  • The slot result is drawn on the server with a cryptographic random number generator the moment a press is accepted. The server then refuses every press until the spin time has passed, so only one spin runs at a time. Your browser plays the reels for the time the server says is left, then adds the result to the list; your own button stays off until your reels stop, so a spin always settles on your screen before you can press again.
  • The reels are plain HTML animated with the Web Animations API. If your device asks for reduced motion, the symbols change without spinning.
  • A strict Content Security Policy only allows scripts, styles and images from this site (postcard images are shown from your browser's own copy), and connections only to this site and the latency test endpoints. There are no inline scripts.

Before you post

Anything you post, attach or draw goes to every connected browser at once and is stored on their devices. It can't be edited, deleted or recalled. Nothing is moderated. Don't share anything private.

Your data

There are no accounts, no cookies and no tracking. Your theme choice, your count of successful slot presses and latency tests, and when your next test is allowed are kept in this browser's local storage. Board messages, postcards, canvas strokes, slot results and latency results are kept in this browser's IndexedDB, up to 10,000 of each, with the oldest removed first. Postcard images are kept up to 256 MB. Slot jackpots are kept separately and never removed unless you clear local history. The articles you opened on the read page are kept in IndexedDB too, up to 1,000, with the least recently read removed first. Messages you posted and results you started are marked as yours only in this browser. Latency results carry only timings: no address, no name and no device details. Rate limits count by network address in the server's memory only; addresses are never saved or shown, and devices sharing one internet connection share one limit.

Location and details

This is optional and off unless you turn it on. The board and the postcard work the same either way, and share one setting. If you tick Attach my location and browser details and your browser grants location permission, every message or postcard you send carries what your browser reports at that moment: latitude, longitude and accuracy, plus altitude, heading and speed when known, your time zone, UTC offset and local time, language, user agent, platform, screen and window size, CPU threads, memory, touch points, color scheme, motion and contrast settings, and connection type. Anyone can open it under the message with Details, and it is kept and offered back like the message itself. Nothing is looked up from it: no maps, no address, no third-party service. The server does not add your network address. Your browser reports these values and the server cannot check them. Untick the box, or block location for this site, to stop. Messages already sent keep their details.

This removes the board, postcard, canvas, slot, latency and reading history and your counts on this device. The next time you open those pages, they fill up again from the server.

Source code

The code is on GitHub under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or later. If you run a modified copy for other people, you have to offer them its source too.
